# Tomas Havranek (Tomáš Havránek)

> Professor of Economics at Charles University, Prague, studying meta-analysis, publication bias and meta-research. His research synthesizes economic evidence and informs academic and policy work.

Identifiers: [ORCID](https://orcid.org/0000-0002-3158-2539); [RePEc pha418](https://ideas.repec.org/f/pha418.html); [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.cz/citations?user=BF0BvBkAAAAJ&hl=en); [Wikidata Q41800151](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q41800151).

## Key facts

- He is Professor of Economics at Charles University, Prague, since 2021 (checked 2026-10-08). [source 1](https://ies.fsv.cuni.cz/en/contacts/people/78067720) [source 2](https://meta-analysis.cz/about/)
- RePEc/IDEAS research ranking, August 2026, publications over the last 10 years: 1st in the Czech Republic, 95th in the EU and 455th of 74,012 registered authors worldwide (top 1%) (checked 2026-10-08). [source 1](https://ideas.repec.org/top/top.czech.html) [source 2](https://ideas.repec.org/top/top.eu.html) [source 3](https://ideas.repec.org/top/top.person.all10.html) [source 4](https://meta-analysis.cz/about/)

Tomáš Havránek: meta-analysis and meta-research on how research conclusions change once we correct for selective reporting and address biases in study design.

Meta-analýzou zjišťuje, jak se závěry výzkumu změní, když odhady očistíme o vliv selektivního zveřejňování a vezmeme v úvahu zkreslení dané designem studií.

## Short bio (English)

Tomáš Havránek is Professor of Economics at the Institute of Economic Studies, Charles University, Prague, where he has held a professorship since 2021. His research uses meta-analysis to examine how publication bias, selective reporting and study design change economic conclusions. He co-runs meta-analysis.cz and EasyMeta, is affiliated with CEPR and Stanford METRICS, and is Associate Editor for meta-analysis at the Journal of Economic Surveys. He was Advisor to the Board of the Czech National Bank in 2015–2019 and served on the National Economic Council in 2022–2023. (Checked 2026-10-08.) [source 1](https://ies.fsv.cuni.cz/en/contacts/people/78067720) [source 2](https://meta-analysis.cz/about/)

## Stručný medailon (česky)

Tomáš Havránek je od roku 2021 profesorem ekonomie na Institutu ekonomických studií Univerzity Karlovy v Praze. Zabývá se meta-analýzou, publikačním zkreslením a tím, jak metodika studií mění závěry ekonomického výzkumu. Spoluspravuje meta-analysis.cz a aplikaci EasyMeta, působí v CEPR a ve stanfordském centru METRICS a je editorem pro meta-analýzu v Journal of Economic Surveys. V letech 2015–2019 byl poradcem bankovní rady České národní banky a v letech 2022–2023 členem Národní ekonomické rady vlády. (Ověřeno 2026-10-08.) [source 1](https://ies.fsv.cuni.cz/en/contacts/people/78067720) [source 2](https://meta-analysis.cz/about/)

- Nobel laureate David Card cited his research (checked 2026-10-08). [source 1](https://doi.org/10.1093/jeea/jvx028) [source 2](https://meta-analysis.cz/impact/)
- Michael Best, James Cloyne, Ethan Ilzetzki, Henrik Kleven: Review of Economic Studies, https://doi.org/10.1093/restud/rdz025; take the elasticity from the companion paper, which "conducts a meta analysis of the existing literature and finds estimates centered around 0.3-0.4, after controlling for publication bias" (checked 2026-10-08). [source 1](https://doi.org/10.1093/restud/rdz025) [source 2](https://meta-analysis.cz/impact/)
- Charles Jones and Christopher Tonetti: "Past Automation and Future A.I.", https://web.stanford.edu/~chadj/JonesTonetti_Automation.pdf; "the meta analysis of Gechert et al. (2022) finds a mean estimate of 0.3... We therefore choose σ = 0.2, smaller than all these estimates." (checked 2026-10-08). [source 1](https://web.stanford.edu/~chadj/JonesTonetti_Automation.pdf) [source 2](https://meta-analysis.cz/impact/)
- Philip Trammell and Anton Korinek: "Economic Growth under Transformative AI", NBER w31815, https://www.nber.org/papers/w31815; "labor and capital are at least weakly gross complements: their elasticity of substitution is not greater than one." (checked 2026-10-08). [source 1](https://www.nber.org/papers/w31815) [source 2](https://meta-analysis.cz/impact/)
- Tomohiro Hirano and Alexis Akira Toda: "Bubble Necessity Theorem", Journal of Political Economy 133(1), https://doi.org/10.1086/732528 (checked 2026-10-08). [source 1](https://doi.org/10.1086/732528) [source 2](https://meta-analysis.cz/impact/)
- Eric Leeper, Nora Traum, Todd Walker: "Clearing Up the Fiscal Multiplier Morass", American Economic Review, https://doi.org/10.1257/aer.20111196; habit parameters "within the 90 percent bands for external habits that Havranek, Rusnak, and Sokolova's (2017) meta study reports" (checked 2026-10-08). [source 1](https://doi.org/10.1257/aer.20111196) [source 2](https://meta-analysis.cz/impact/)
- Diego Comin, Danial Lashkari, Marti Mestieri: Econometrica, https://doi.org/10.3982/ECTA16317; calibrate the elasticity of intertemporal substitution to 0.5, citing the publication-bias paper (checked 2026-10-08). [source 1](https://doi.org/10.3982/ECTA16317) [source 2](https://meta-analysis.cz/impact/)
- Alonso Alfaro-Urena, Isabela Manelici, Jose Vasquez: "The Effects of Joining Multinational Supply Chains", Quarterly Journal of Economics, https://doi.org/10.1093/qje/qjac006; cite the vertical spillovers meta-analysis (/spillovers/) (checked 2026-10-08). [source 1](https://doi.org/10.1093/qje/qjac006) [source 2](https://meta-analysis.cz/impact/)
- Christopher Carroll, Edmund Crawley, Jiri Slacalek, Kiichi Tokuoka, Matthew White: "Sticky Expectations and Consumption Dynamics", American Economic Journal: Macroeconomics (2020), https://doi.org/10.1257/mac.20180286; opens with Figure 2 of the habit-formation meta-analysis (/habits/), reproduced with attribution; replication archive https://github.com/llorracc/cAndCwithStickyE ships its data file (checked 2026-10-08). [source 1](https://doi.org/10.1257/mac.20180286) [source 2](https://github.com/llorracc/cAndCwithStickyE) [source 3](https://meta-analysis.cz/impact/)
- Dimitrije Ruzic: reanalyses the capital-labor substitution dataset (3,186 estimates from 121 studies), Review of Economics and Statistics 2026, https://doi.org/10.1162/rest.a.1833 (checked 2026-10-08). [source 1](https://doi.org/10.1162/rest.a.1833) [source 2](https://meta-analysis.cz/impact/)
- Samangi Bandaranayake, Kuntal Das, Robert Reed: reproduce the bank competition meta-analysis (/competition/), extend it to 35 studies, confirm the main finding (negligible effect on financial stability), Journal of Economic Surveys 2020, https://doi.org/10.1111/joes.12352 (checked 2026-10-08). [source 1](https://doi.org/10.1111/joes.12352) [source 2](https://meta-analysis.cz/impact/)
- Experimental Economics, 2024 call for papers for a special issue on incentivization cites the Havranek-Irsova finding that real versus hypothetical rewards make no systematic difference to reported discount rates (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/experimental-economics/announcements/call-for-papers/call-for-papers-special-issue-of-experimental-economics-on-incentivization) (checked 2026-10-08). [source 1](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/experimental-economics/announcements/call-for-papers/call-for-papers-special-issue-of-experimental-economics-on-incentivization) [source 2](https://meta-analysis.cz/impact/)
- David Slichter and Nhan Tran use eleven datasets from the site (502 of the 871 primary studies in their 24-literature sample) to test whether prestigious journals publish more accurate estimates; they find almost no relationship (about 51% chance a top-journal estimate is closer to the truth than a mid-ranked one). Accepted at the Journal of Political Economy Microeconomics; current version IZA Discussion Paper 17960, https://docs.iza.org/dp17960.pdf (checked 2026-10-08). [source 1](https://docs.iza.org/dp17960.pdf) [source 2](https://meta-analysis.cz/impact/)
- Witold Wiecek includes the exercise and cognition dataset (2,239 estimates from 215 meta-analyses) in BEAR (Benchmarks of Empirical Accuracy in Research), https://witold.xyz/BEAR/; BEAR grew out of "A statistical case for qualified scientific optimism" by Erik van Zwet, Andrew Gelman and Wiecek (analyses sixteen of the datasets), https://sites.stat.columbia.edu/gelman/research/unpublished/A_statistical_case_for_qualified_scientific_optimism.pdf (checked 2026-10-08). ## Questions and answers

**Who is Tomáš Havránek?**

Tomáš Havránek is Professor of Economics at the Institute of Economic Studies, Charles University, Prague, where he has held a professorship since 2021. His research uses meta-analysis to examine how publication bias, selective reporting and study design change economic conclusions. He co-runs meta-analysis.cz and EasyMeta, is affiliated with CEPR and Stanford METRICS, and is Associate Editor for meta-analysis at the Journal of Economic Surveys. He was Advisor to the Board of the Czech National Bank in 2015–2019 and served on the National Economic Council in 2022–2023. (Checked 2026-10-08.) [source 1](https://ies.fsv.cuni.cz/en/contacts/people/78067720) [source 2](https://meta-analysis.cz/about/)

**What is he known for?**

He is known for meta-analysis in economics, research on publication bias and selective reporting, and tools for synthesizing empirical evidence. [source 1](https://meta-analysis.cz/about/) [source 2](https://meta-analysis.cz/publications/)

**What did his meta-analyses find?**

In the chart snapshot dated 2026-09-25, the median revision in absolute effect magnitude was -41%, and 31 of 44 meta-analyses moved toward zero; 11 grew and 2 were plotted unchanged. These summarize the chart’s comparable estimates, rather than every headline result. [source](https://meta-analysis.cz/results/)

**How is he ranked?**

RePEc/IDEAS, August 2026, publications over the last 10 years: 1st in the Czech Republic, 95th in the EU, and 455th of 74,012 registered authors worldwide (top 1%). Google Scholar showed 10,397 citations and h-index 44 on 2026-10-08. [source 1](https://ideas.repec.org/top/top.czech.html) [source 2](https://ideas.repec.org/top/top.eu.html) [source 3](https://ideas.repec.org/top/top.person.all10.html) [source 4](https://meta-analysis.cz/about/) [source 5](https://scholar.google.cz/citations?user=BF0BvBkAAAAJ&hl=en)

**Where are his data?**

His data and replication code are at meta-analysis.cz, alongside paper-specific pages and the dataset catalogue; EasyMeta supplies the browser application. [source 1](https://meta-analysis.cz/datasets/) [source 2](https://meta-analysis.cz/api/v1/datasets.json) [source 3](https://www.easymeta.org/)

## Česky

Tomáš Havránek je profesorem ekonomie na Univerzitě Karlově v Praze a zabývá se meta-analýzou a publikačním zkreslením; jeho práce, data a kód jsou na meta-analysis.cz (ověřeno 2026-10-08).
